title: How universities can lead the way towards a sustainable future
desc:
Join the launch of our Sustainable Imperial Strategy (2026–2031) .

As a community of thinkers, teachers, professionals and innovators – how do we best translat e our sustainability ideas into real work i mpact? How do we bring our ingenuity to guide our institution and the world beyond to a more sustainable future?

Whether you are deeply involved in sustainability or just starting out, you are a vital part of our collective journey towards a more sustainable Imperial and planet.

Across a short presentation, an exhibition showcase, and networking afternoon tea, you’ll meet the staff, students, alumni and community members bringing our sustainability ambitions to reality – and learn how you can get involved.

Join us as we unveil our vision for the next five years and beyond.

title: Weird Weather: The Response by David Shukman
desc:
Join David Shukman, former BBC Science Editor, and Theodore Keeping, wildfire & climate scientist at World Weather Attribution, Imperial College London, for a conversation around how climate change is reshaping our world through increasingly erratic and extreme weather, and how we can respond.

​David’s latest book, The Response: A Story of Fire and Flood in Britain’s New World of Extremes , is a gripping account of the new extremes that our bodies, buildings and landscapes now face in Britain and around the world, compiled through extensive interviews with experts, including researchers from Imperial. The discussion will explore themes from the book, notably wildfires, and the role of communication in driving climate action.

David will also be signing books after the talks. Please note…

title: IDE Seminar Series – Dr Shevanthi Nayagam
desc:
Challenges and opportunities in Hepatitis B elimination

Chronic hepatitis B remains a major cause of global mortality, despite the availability of effective vaccines and antiviral therapies. The burden falls disproportionately on LMICs, where significant barriers persist in achieving equitable access to the interventions needed for elimination.

In this seminar, I will discuss progress towards hepatitis B elimination and the opportunities and challenges that remain. Using examples from clinical epidemiology, modelling and health-economic analyses, I will explore how interdisciplinary approaches can help inform implementation, policy development and future research priorities across diverse settings.

title: History of Interdisciplinary Education Symposium
desc:
In collaboration with the History of Education Society , this day-long symposium at Imperial , on Wednesday 17 June 2026, will bring together researchers and educators interested in the history of education, specifically interdisciplinary higher education in the UK and beyond.

While interdisciplinary education at Imperial College London has increased in recent years, particularly with the foundation of I-Explore in 2019 , more widely, interdisciplinary HE has undergone significant changes.

Key interdisciplinary institutions and academic initiatives, including at Keele, Sussex and York, have fallen back into traditional disciplinary boundaries, reflecting convergence in a once diverse tertiary sector. Simultaneously, innovations in higher education are addressing interdisciplinary…
